access_links.label: Data paper: An update on global mining land use (Scientific Data, 2022)

description: This dataset maps the land used by the global mining industry as 44,929 polygons covering 101,583 square kilometres, including large-scale and artisanal and small-scale mining. It was produced by Victor Maus and colleagues at the Vienna University of Economics and Business and IIASA to quantify mining land use, and published on PANGAEA on 14 March 2022 as an update of Version 1. Polygons include open cuts, tailings dams, waste rock dumps, water ponds and processing infrastructure, digitised by visual interpretation of the 2019 Sentinel-2 cloudless mosaic at 10 m resolution within 10 km of the 34,820 mine coordinates of the S&P metals and mining database. Files are a GeoPackage of polygons in WGS84 with country code and area, a CSV summary per country, gridded mining area at 30 arc-seconds, 5 arc-minutes and 30 arc-minutes, and 1,000 validation control points; download is free under CC-BY-SA-4.0. Caveats: the search area depends on a commercial mine list, so mines absent from it are missed; the reported overall accuracy is 88.3 percent with producer's accuracy of 78.9 percent for the mine class, and the snapshot is 2019. For simulation it gives the footprint of mining assets for hazard exposure, land-use and environmental impact studies. The data paper is Maus et al. (2022), Scientific Data 9, 433. Related catalogue records include the USGS Mineral Resources Data System and the Global Tailings Portal.
